<thought>Using the ESI mass spectrum, the base peak at m/z 199.00 corresponds to the [M+H]⁺ ion. Subtracting the mass of a proton gives a neutral mass of ~197.99 Da. The isotopic pattern (two nearly equal peaks 2 Da apart) indicates the presence of a bromine atom. Accounting for Br (monoisotopic mass 78.918 Da) leaves a residual mass of ~119.07 Da, which matches the composition C₅H₁₁O₃ (exact mass 119.074 Da). Combining this with Br gives the molecular formula C₅H₁₁O₃Br, which fits the observed m/z within experimental error.</thought>
<final_answer>C5H11O3Br</final_answer>
